hints: Begin with the angle-addition identity for $\sin(2x+x)$.
Replace $\sin2x$ by $2\sin x\cos x$ and $\cos2x$ by $1-2\sin^2x$.
Use $\cos^2x=1-\sin^2x$ in the remaining product and collect powers of $\sin x$ to reach the identity.
walkthrough:
Apply the addition formula $\sin(A + B) = \sin A\cos B + \cos A\sin B$ with $A = 2x$ and $B = x$:
$$\sin 3x = \sin(2x + x) = \sin 2x\cos x + \cos 2x\sin x$$

Substitute the double angle formulas $\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x$ and $\cos 2x = 1 - 2\sin^2 x$:
$$\sin 3x = (2\sin x\cos x)\cos x + (1 - 2\sin^2 x)\sin x$$
$$= 2\sin x\cos^2 x + \sin x - 2\sin^3 x$$

Substitute the Pythagorean identity $\cos^2 x = 1 - \sin^2 x$:
$$\sin 3x = 2\sin x(1 - \sin^2 x) + \sin x - 2\sin^3 x$$

Expand and collect like powers of $\sin x$:
$$\sin 3x = 2\sin x - 2\sin^3 x + \sin x - 2\sin^3 x$$
$$= (2\sin x + \sin x) - (2\sin^3 x + 2\sin^3 x)$$
$$= 3\sin x - 4\sin^3 x$$
This establishes the identity $\sin 3x \equiv 3\sin x - 4\sin^3 x$ as required.

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Identities: Gives the expansion of $\sin(2x+x)$. Applies trigonometric formulae and Pythagoras to express $\sin3x$ in terms of $\sin x$. The final result is $\sin3x\equiv3\sin x-4\sin^3x$.

hints: Rearrange the identity from part (i) to express $\sin^3x$ as a linear combination of $\sin x$ and $\sin3x$.
Integrate both sine terms, remembering the factor $1/3$ when integrating $\sin3x$.
Evaluate the resulting cosine expression at $x=\pi/3$ and $x=0$, keeping all values exact.
walkthrough:
Rearrange the identity from part (i) to express $\sin^3 x$ in terms of single-power trigonometric functions:
$$\sin 3x = 3\sin x - 4\sin^3 x$$
$$4\sin^3 x = 3\sin x - \sin 3x$$
$$\sin^3 x = \dfrac{3}{4}\sin x - \dfrac{1}{4}\sin 3x$$

Substitute this expression into the definite integral:
$$\int_0^{\frac{1}{3}\pi} \sin^3 x\,\mathrm{d}x = \int_0^{\frac{1}{3}\pi} \left(\dfrac{3}{4}\sin x - \dfrac{1}{4}\sin 3x\right)\mathrm{d}x$$

Integrate each term with respect to $x$:
$$\int \sin x\,\mathrm{d}x = -\cos x$$
$$\int \sin 3x\,\mathrm{d}x = -\dfrac{1}{3}\cos 3x$$
Therefore:
$$\left[-\dfrac{3}{4}\cos x + \dfrac{1}{12}\cos 3x\right]_0^{\frac{1}{3}\pi}$$

Evaluate at the upper limit $x = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi$:
$$\cos\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\pi\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}, \quad \cos\left(3 \times \dfrac{1}{3}\pi\right) = \cos\pi = -1$$
$$\text{At } x = \dfrac{1}{3}\pi: \quad -\dfrac{3}{4}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + \dfrac{1}{12}(-1) = -\dfrac{3}{8} - \dfrac{1}{12} = -\dfrac{9}{24} - \dfrac{2}{24} = -\dfrac{11}{24}$$

Evaluate at the lower limit $x = 0$:
$$\cos 0 = 1, \quad \cos(3 \times 0) = \cos 0 = 1$$
$$\text{At } x = 0: \quad -\dfrac{3}{4}(1) + \dfrac{1}{12}(1) = -\dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{1}{12} = -\dfrac{18}{24} + \dfrac{2}{24} = -\dfrac{16}{24}$$

Subtract the lower limit value from the upper limit value:
$$\text{Integral} = \left(-\dfrac{11}{24}\right) - \left(-\dfrac{16}{24}\right) = -\dfrac{11}{24} + \dfrac{16}{24} = \dfrac{5}{24}$$
The exact value is $\dfrac{5}{24}$.

ai_rubric.Integration: Applies the identity, integrate, and derives $-\dfrac34\cos x+\dfrac1{12}\cos3x$; Applies the limits in an integral of the form $a\cos x+b\cos3x$, where $ab\ne0$; Derives $\dfrac5{24}$.
